stages.name: Neutral & independent
stages.desc: Neutral states and peoples outside the war's alliances

stages.name: Macedon & allies
stages.desc: Philip V's kingdom and the Greek states of his Hellenic League

stages.name: Aetolian League
stages.desc: The Aetolian federation, Macedon's rival, and the lands it held

stages.name: Rome & allies
stages.desc: Rome, its Italian allies, provinces and protectorates

stages.name: Carthage & allies
stages.desc: Carthage, and the peoples of Italy and Sicily who sided with Hannibal

stages.name: Illyrian kingdoms
stages.desc: The Illyrian kings of the Adriatic coast

states.name: West Macedonia
timeline: Upper Macedonia: the hill cantons of Orestis, Elimeia and Lyncus, under the Macedonian crown

states.name: Epirus
timeline: The Epirote League, a member of Philip's Hellenic League
Aetolian raiders burn the sanctuary of Zeus at Dodona
Epirote magistrates broker the peace between Philip and Rome at Phoenice

states.name: Centre Macedonia
timeline: Pella and Thessalonica: the heart of the young Philip V's kingdom
Philip spends the winter building a fleet of a hundred light warships

states.name: East Macedonia and Thrace
timeline: Amphipolis and the Strymon valley, Macedonian since Philip II

states.name: Mount Athos
timeline: The Athos peninsula of Chalcidice, Macedonian territory

states.name: Thessalia
timeline: Thessaly, ruled from Macedon; the fortress of Demetrias is one of the 'fetters of Greece'
Philip shuttles from Demetrias to answer raids by Attalus and the Romans

states.name: Central Greece
timeline: The Aetolian League holds Phthiotis, Doris and western Locris; Boeotia and Euboea side with Macedon
Rome and the Aetolians storm Anticyra; its people are enslaved
Philip defeats the Aetolians and their allies twice near Lamia
Attalus and the Romans sack Oreus and Opus; Philip nearly captures Attalus
Left alone by Rome, the Aetolians make a separate peace with Philip

states.name: Attica
timeline: Athens keeps out of the wars of the Greeks
Athens joins Egypt, Rhodes and Chios in trying to broker peace

states.name: Peloponnese
timeline: The Achaean League and Macedonian-held Corinth; Sparta and Elis back the Aetolians
Philip ravages Messenia, alarming his Achaean allies
Philopoemen's Achaeans defeat Sparta at Mantinea

states.name: West Greece
timeline: Aetolia, heartland of the Aetolian League; Achaea and Acarnania stand with Macedon
Philip sacks Thermum, the Aetolians' federal sanctuary
Peace of Naupactus: Agelaus warns of the 'cloud in the west'
The Aetolian League makes an alliance with Rome against Philip
Abandoned by Rome, the Aetolians accept Philip's terms

states.name: Crete
timeline: Cretan cities supply archers and mercenaries to every side

states.name: South Aegean
timeline: Rhodes and the Cyclades: Rhodes, a neutral sea power, guards Aegean trade
Rhodian envoys try to end the war in Greece

states.name: North Aegean
timeline: Lesbos and Chios are independent; only small Lemnos is Macedonian
A Roman and Pergamene fleet fails to take Lemnos

states.name: Ionian Islands
timeline: Corcyra, under Roman protection since 229 BC
Laevinus takes Zacynthus and winters his fleet at Corcyra
A Carthaginian fleet sails to Corcyra to aid Philip, but the two never join

states.name: Valle d'Aosta
timeline: Alpine valleys of the Salassi, outside Roman rule

states.name: Piemonte
timeline: Ligurian and Gallic tribes such as the Taurini
Hannibal comes down from the Alps and storms the Taurini's chief town

states.name: Lombardia
timeline: The Insubres, defeated by Rome in 222 BC
The Insubres rise and join Hannibal

states.name: Trentino-Alto Adige
timeline: Alpine peoples beyond Roman rule

states.name: Liguria
timeline: Ligurian hill tribes, outside Roman rule
Mago, Hannibal's brother, lands at Genua and raises the Ligurians

states.name: Emilia-Romagna
timeline: Lands of the Boii; Rome is founding a colony at Placentia
The Boii revolt; Hannibal wins at the Trebia in December

states.name: Marche
timeline: Picenum, Roman and allied land
Hannibal's brother Hasdrubal is defeated and killed at the Metaurus

states.name: Veneto
timeline: The Veneti, allies of Rome

states.name: Friuli-Venezia Giulia
timeline: Carnic and Venetic lands at the edge of Roman influence

states.name: Abruzzo
timeline: Marsi, Paeligni and Vestini, Rome's Italian allies
After Trasimene, Hannibal marches through to the Adriatic

states.name: Molise
timeline: The Pentri Samnites, who stay loyal to Rome

states.name: Apulia
timeline: Daunian and Messapian towns allied to Rome
After Cannae, Arpi, Salapia and other towns go over to Hannibal
Tarentum is betrayed to Hannibal
Fabius retakes Tarentum; Rome regains Apulia

states.name: Basilicata
timeline: The Lucanians, allies of Rome
Most of the Lucanians go over to Hannibal
The Lucanians surrender to Rome

states.name: Calabria
timeline: The Bruttii and the Greek cities of the south, allies of Rome
The Bruttii join Hannibal; Locri and Croton follow in 215 BC
Philip's envoys land near the temple of Hera on Cape Lacinium
Scipio retakes Locri; Hannibal holds out in Bruttium

states.name: Campania
timeline: Capua, Italy's second city, bound to Rome
Capua opens its gates to Hannibal
In Hannibal's camp, the alliance with Philip is sworn
Rome retakes Capua and executes its leaders

states.name: Lazio
timeline: Rome and Latium
The captured envoys are brought to Rome in chains
Hannibal marches to the walls of Rome, then turns away

states.name: Toscana
timeline: Etruscan cities, allies of Rome

states.name: Sicily
timeline: Roman province in the west; Hiero II's Syracuse, Rome's ally, in the east
Syracuse breaks with Rome; Carthage sends an army to Sicily
Marcellus takes Syracuse; Archimedes is killed
Agrigentum falls; all Sicily is Roman

states.name: Sardegna
timeline: Roman province since 238 BC
A Sardinian revolt backed by a Carthaginian army is crushed

states.name: Umbria
timeline: Umbrian allies of Rome
Hannibal destroys a Roman army at Lake Trasimene

states.name: North Macedonia
timeline: Paeonia, Macedon's northern march against the Dardanians
Raids from the north call Philip home from the war in Greece

states.name: Albania
timeline: The Illyrian kingdom in the north; Apollonia and Epidamnus under Roman protection on the coast
Rome defeats Demetrius of Pharos, who flees to Philip; its protectorate is restored
Surprised at Apollonia, Philip burns his fleet on the Aoös
Philip seizes Dimale, the Parthini, Atintania and Lissus
Peace of Phoenice: the Parthini and Dimale return to Rome; Philip keeps Atintania

states.name: Turkey
timeline: Western Anatolia: Attalus I of Pergamon, Prusias I of Bithynia and Seleucid lands
Attalus of Pergamon joins Rome and the Aetolians against Philip
Prusias of Bithynia, Philip's ally, attacks Pergamon; Attalus sails home

states.name: Tunisia
timeline: Carthage and its African heartland
Carthage braces for Scipio's invasion of Africa

states.name: Montenegro
timeline: The Illyrian kingdom of Scerdilaidas around the Bay of Rhizon
Scerdilaidas and his son Pleuratus join Rome's alliance against Philip

events.title: Social War
events.text: Philip V, eighteen, leads his Hellenic League into war against the Aetolian League.

events.title: Dodona burned
events.text: Aetolian raiders burn the sanctuary of Zeus at Dodona, the oldest oracle in Greece.

events.title: Demetrius flees
events.text: Rome defeats Demetrius of Pharos at Dimale and Pharos; he takes refuge at Philip's court.

events.title: Thermum sacked
events.text: Philip storms Thermum, the Aetolians' federal sanctuary, and burns its stoas and offerings.

events.title: Over the Alps
events.text: Hannibal comes down into Italy with some twenty-six thousand men and storms the Taurini's town.

events.title: The Trebia
events.text: Hannibal defeats a Roman consular army on the Trebia in December; the Gauls rally to him.

events.title: Lake Trasimene
events.text: Hannibal ambushes and destroys the army of the consul Flaminius by the lake shore.

events.title: News at Nemea
events.text: Watching the Nemean Games, Philip reads of Trasimene; Demetrius urges him to look to Italy.

events.title: Peace of Naupactus
events.text: Philip ends the Social War; Agelaus warns the Greeks of the 'cloud in the west'.

events.title: The fleet turns back
events.text: Philip's hundred light warships near Apollonia flee home at a false report of a Roman fleet.

events.title: Cannae
events.text: On the second of August, Hannibal annihilates the largest army Rome had ever fielded.

events.title: Capua defects
events.text: Italy's second city opens its gates to Hannibal.

events.title: Envoys land
events.text: Xenophanes of Athens, Philip's envoy, lands near the temple of Hera on Cape Lacinium.

events.title: Bluffing Laevinus
events.text: Stopped near Luceria, Xenophanes says he has come to ally with Rome, and is waved on.

events.title: The oath
events.text: In Hannibal's camp, Hannibal and Xenophanes swear an alliance before the gods of both peoples.

events.title: Envoys captured
events.text: Sailing home with Hannibal's envoys, Xenophanes is caught by Roman ships off the heel of Italy.

events.title: Letters to Rome
events.text: The treaty and Hannibal's letter reach the Senate; the Carthaginians are kept in chains.

events.title: Sardinia revolts
events.text: A Sardinian rising backed by a Carthaginian army is crushed by Titus Manlius Torquatus.

events.title: Fleet burned
events.text: Surprised by a Roman night attack at Apollonia, Philip burns his fleet and marches home.

events.title: Syracuse breaks away
events.text: Hippocrates and Epicydes take Syracuse over to Carthage; Marcellus begins a long siege.

events.title: Messene ravaged
events.text: Philip ravages Messenia, turning his Achaean allies against him.

events.title: Aratus dies
events.text: Aratus of Sicyon, Philip's old adviser, dies; many believe Philip had him poisoned.

events.title: Lissus taken
events.text: Marching overland, Philip storms the citadel of Lissus and reaches the Adriatic.

events.title: Tarentum betrayed
events.text: Young Tarentines open the city to Hannibal; the Roman garrison holds the citadel.

events.title: Syracuse falls
events.text: Marcellus storms Syracuse; Archimedes, whose machines held the walls, is killed.

events.title: Rome and Aetolia
events.text: The Aetolian League allies with Rome: Aetolia takes the land, Rome the captives and booty.

events.title: Hannibal at the gates
events.text: Hannibal marches on Rome to save Capua, then turns away.

events.title: Capua falls
events.text: Rome retakes Capua and executes its leading men.

events.title: Zacynthus seized
events.text: Laevinus takes Zacynthus, except its citadel, and winters at Corcyra.

events.title: Anticyra enslaved
events.text: Laevinus and the Aetolians take Anticyra; Rome enslaves its people.

events.title: Aegina sold
events.text: Rome and the Aetolians take Aegina and sell it to Attalus of Pergamon for thirty talents.

events.title: Agrigentum falls
events.text: Carthage's last stronghold in Sicily is betrayed to Laevinus.

events.title: Battles at Lamia
events.text: Philip twice defeats the Aetolians and their Roman and Pergamene auxiliaries.

events.title: Tarentum retaken
events.text: The aged Fabius Maximus recovers Tarentum, Hannibal's prize port.

events.title: Punic fleet at Corcyra
events.text: A Carthaginian fleet sails to Corcyra to join Philip, but turns back without meeting him.

events.title: Attalus escapes
events.text: Philip surprises Attalus plundering Opus; the king barely reaches his ships.

events.title: The Metaurus
events.text: Hannibal's brother Hasdrubal, bringing a second army to Italy, is defeated and killed.

events.title: Mantinea
events.text: Philopoemen's Achaeans, Philip's allies, defeat Sparta and kill its regent Machanidas.

events.title: Aetolia makes peace
events.text: Left alone by Rome, the Aetolians accept a separate peace on Philip's terms.

events.title: Sempronius lands
events.text: A Roman army of eleven thousand men lands at Epidamnus, too late to change the war.

events.title: Peace of Phoenice
events.text: Philip and Rome make peace in Epirus; Rome keeps its coastal protectorate.

events.title: Mago at Genua
events.text: Hannibal's brother Mago lands in Liguria; no help comes from Macedon.

chartNote: Share of the map's area by the side each present-day region mainly stood on: Greece's and Italy's regions, Albania, North Macedonia, Montenegro, Tunisia, and Turkey west of 30°E. Regions are today's boundaries; most held cities on both sides, so the map shows the dominant power. It is a simplification.
